Concepts
Editorial, Jim Melton, 2021-05-30
What is SQL?
Editorial, Jim Melton, 2021-05-30
The name SQL is correctly pronounced ess cue ell, instead of the somewhat common sequel. SQL, specified in the parts of the ISO/IEC 9075 series, is a database language (more precisely, a data sublanguage) used for access to pseudo-relational databases that are managed by pseudo-relational database management systems (RDBMS).
Editorial, Jim Melton, 2021-05-30 Editorial: Stephen Cannan, 2022-03-20 WG3:W20-010 P00-USA-310 Many books and articles define SQL by parenthetically claiming that the letters stand for Structured Query Language. While this was undoubtedly true for the original prototypes, it is not true of the standard. When the letters appear in product names, they have often been assigned this meaning by the product implementers, but users are ill-served by claims that the word structured accurately describes the language. In the SQL standard, the letters do not stand for anything at all. There are afficionados who assert that the letters stand for SQL Query Language, a recursive acronym in the tradition of GNU (GNU’s Not Unix) and SPARQL (SPARQL Protocol And RDF Query Language).
Editorial, Jim Melton, 2021-05-30
SQL is based on, but is not a strict implementation of, the relational model of data (see ), making SQL pseudo-relational instead of truly relational. There are two principal ways in which SQL breaks from the relational model.
Editorial, Jim Melton, 2021-05-30
The relational model requires that every relationTerms defined by the relational model are used correctly in this Subclause, but are not defined or explained in this document; readers are referred to the formal specification of the relational model. have no duplicate rows (that is, rows for which all corresponding attributes have equal values). A consequence of this requirement is that every relation has a primary key. SQL does not enforce this requirement, but provides syntax that permits application developers to enforce the requirement as needed.
Editorial, Jim Melton, 2021-05-30
The relational model does not specify or recognize any sort of flag or other marker that represents unspecified, unknown, or otherwise missing data values. Consequently, the relational model depends only on two-valued (true/false) logic. SQL provides a null value that serves this purpose. In support of null values, SQL also depends on three-valued (true/false/unknown) logic.
Editorial, Jim Melton, 2021-05-30
The SQL standard defines two distinct aspects of the language: a data definition language (known in the standard as a schema manipulation language) that supports the creation and destruction of database objects, such as tables, columns, and integrity constraints; and a data manipulation language that allows the retrieval, creation, modification, and deletion of data.
Editorial, Jim Melton, 2021-05-30
An especially important characteristic of SQL is that it is declarative (as opposed to procedural) in nature.ISO/IEC 9075-4, specifies a number of SQL statements that provide a procedural capability through which procedures and functions can be written entirely in SQL. Procedural programs can also be written in ordinary host programming languages with embedded SQL statements. That is, SQLs syntax and semantics allow application writers to specify the rules by which results may be computed by an SQL system, rather than specifying the algorithms by which those results must be computed. This contrasts with earlier database languages that required the details specification of step-by-step algorithms to retrieve, filter, and format the data required by applications.

SQL-agents
DBL:LGW-027R2/X3H2-97-146
An SQL-agent is that which causes the execution of SQL-statements. In the case of the direct invocation of SQL (see ), it is . Alter­natively, it may consist of one or more compilation units that, when executed, invoke externally-invoked procedures in an SQL-client module.
SQL-implementations
Jim Melton, 2020-09-04, Eliminate "hanging paragraphs" per Directives, Part 2
Introduction to SQL-implementations
DBL:LGW-027R2/X3H2-97-146 Editorial: Stephen Cannan, 2022-03-20 WG3:W20-010 P00-USA-309
An SQL-implementation is a processor that executes SQL-statements, as required by the SQL-agent. An SQL-implementation, as perceived by the SQL-agent, includes one SQL-client, to which that SQL-agent is bound, and one or more SQL-servers. An SQL-implementation is able to conform to ISO/IEC 9075 without allowing more than one SQL-server to exist in an SQL-environment.
DBL:LGW-027R2/X3H2-97-146 Email from Phil Brown, 2006-12-11 Editorial: Stephen Cannan, 2022-03-20 WG3:W20-010 P00-USA-310
Because an SQL-implementation can be specified only in terms of how it executes SQL-statements, the concept denotes an installed instance of some software (database management system). ISO/IEC 9075 does not distinguish between features of the SQL-implementation that are determined by the software implementer and those determined by the installer.
DBL:LGW-027R2/X3H2-97-146 Editorial: Stephen Cannan, 2022-03-20 WG3:W20-010 P00-USA-310
ISO/IEC 9075 recognizes that SQL-client and SQL-server software may have been obtained from different implementers; it does not specify the method of communication between SQL-client and SQL-server.
SQL-clients
DBL:LGW-027R2/X3H2-97-146 FCD1/1998 CAN-P01-002 Editorial: Stephen Cannan, 2022-02-24 W20-010 P00-USA-312
An SQL-client is a processor, perceived by the SQL-agent to be part of the SQL-implementation, that establishes SQL-connections between itself and SQL-servers and maintains a diagnostics area and other state data relating to interactions between itself, the SQL-agent, and the SQL-servers.
WG3:DRS-050/H2-2002-___ FDIS1SP1, 2003
When one or more SQL-connections have been established for an SQL-client, the diagnostics area maintained by that SQL-client is a copy of the first diagnostics area in the diagnostics area stack (see ) maintained by the SQL-server of the current SQL-connection. When no SQL-connection exists, the diagnostics area is either empty or contains diagnostics information pertaining to some failed SQL-connection.
SQL-servers
DBL:LGW-027R2/X3H2-97-146 Editorial: Stephen Cannan, 2022-02-24 W20-010 P00-USA-314
Each SQL-server is a processor, perceived by the SQL-agent to be part of the SQL-implementation, that manages SQL-data.
DBL:LGW-027R2/X3H2-97-146
Each SQL-server:
manages the SQL-session taking place over the SQL-connection between itself and the SQL-client;
executes SQL-statements received from the SQL-client, receiving and sending data as required;
maintains the state of the SQL-session, including the authorization identifier and certain session defaults.
SQL-client modules
DBL:LGW-027R2/X3H2-97-146
An SQL-client module is a module that is explicitly created and dropped by mechanisms.
DBL:LGW-027R2/X3H2-97-146
An SQL-client module does not necessarily have a name; if it does, the permitted names are .
DBL:LGW-027R2/X3H2-97-146 WG3:DRS-068/H2-2002-___
An SQL-client module contains zero or more externally-invoked procedures. An externally-invoked procedure consists of a single SQL-statement. An externally-invoked procedure is invoked from a compilation unit of a host language.

DBL:LGW-027R2/X3H2-97-146
A referential constraint specifies one or more columns as referencing columns and corresponding referenced columns in some (not necessarily distinct) base table, referred to as the referenced table. Such referenced columns are the unique columns of some unique constraint of the referenced table. A referential constraint is always satisfied if, for every row in the referencing table, the values of the referencing columns are equal to those of the corresponding referenced columns of some row in the referenced table. If null values are present, however, satisfaction of the referential constraint depends on the treatment specified for nulls (known as the match type).

Every isolation level guarantees that every SQL-transaction is executed; SQL-transactions not executing completely fail completely. Every isolation level guarantees that no update is lost. The highest isolation level, SERIALIZABLE, guarantees serializable execution, meaning that the effect of SQL-transactions that overlap in time is the same as the effect they would have had, had they not overlapped in time. The other levels of isolation, REPEATABLE READ, READ COMMITTED, and READ UNCOMMITTED, guarantee progressively lower degrees of isolation.

Editorial: Stephen Cannan, 2023-07-10, Standardize the spelling of keyword
Keywords and s
In the text (including the Format sections) of the ISO/IEC 9075 series, certain syntax elements are used to specify SQL statements and parts of SQL expressions. Those syntax elements are called keywords. They are used either to identify the SQL statement being specified or to identify details of the syntax of statements and expressions.
In the ISO/IEC 9075 series, the word keyword is used to refer to those syntax elements, and the BNF non-terminal symbol is used when the definition or use of a keyword in a Format is referenced. Throughout the ISO/IEC 9075 series, all keywords are specified using only upper-case letters; for example, SELECT is a keyword.
In SQL syntax, a keyword spelled using one or more lower-case letters is equivalent to spelling it with every lower-case letter replaced with its corresponding upper-case letter. For example, sELecT, when used as a keyword, is identical in effect to SELECT.
